title: China: weak domestic demand and property investment slump
what_happened: October 2026 data showed retail sales growth of 0.4% year over year, fixed-asset investment down 8.1% for January to October, and property development investment down 21.6%.
how_it_reaches_markets: Weaker demand for commodities and for foreign companies selling into China; pressure on Chinese and Hong Kong shares; deflationary pressure exported through cheap goods, which also feeds the tariff dispute.

sourced_facts.text: October 2026: value added of industry above designated size +4.8% y/y; retail sales of consumer goods +0.4% y/y (National Bureau of Statistics, released 2026-11-16)
September 2026, for comparison: industry +5.5% y/y; retail sales +1.1% y/y (National Bureau of Statistics, released 2026-10-19)
January to October 2026: fixed-asset investment -8.1% y/y; real estate development investment -21.6% y/y (National Bureau of Statistics)

resolved_when_all: Retail sales growth above 3% year over year for three consecutive months
Year-to-date property development investment decline narrower than 10%
worsened_when_any: Retail sales fall year over year
A large developer or local-government financing vehicle defaults on a public bond

relief_headlines_that_do_not_resolve_it: Announcements of stimulus without subsequent improvement in the monthly data
